title: Artifact import & assurance pipeline with deterministic conversion and stable pin recommendation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an end-to-end artifact import and assurance pipeline focused on deterministic conversion, license/safety checks, and an automated stable-pin recommendation. This ticket scopes the orchestrator that wires together the signed-manifest ingress, conversion workers (quantization + kernel mapping), deterministic hash verification, compatibility test-suite, safety sandboxing, and the pin-recommendation service which produces a versioned profile published to the model catalog.
acceptance_criteria: Artifacts can be ingested via signed manifest and stored in artifact-bucket with provenance metadata
Conversion worker produces reproducible binaries with content-addressable hashes across two independent runs
Compatibility suite runs automatically and reports pass/fail for CPU/GPU variants within 4 hours of ingestion
Safety checks (license scan, opt-out tokens, basic toxic output classifier) must pass before pin recommendation
Pin recommendation output includes perf profile (latency P50/P95, memory footprint, token throughput), quantization level, and suggested runtime target
Profile publisher emits a versioned manifest to the model-catalog and can toggle canary rollout to dedicated capacity
Rollback gating prevents publishing when any critical test fails and surfaces actionable errors in the console
work_log: 2025-02-20: Ticket created by Aisha outlining scope and deliverables.
2025-02-24: Initial design sync with infra and runtime teams — agreed on signed-manifest format and required provenance fields (uploader, source_url, license).
2025-02-26: PoC conversion worker produced deterministic quantized artifacts for small llama-like model on x86 GPU; observed nondeterminism in operator ordering.
2025-02-28: Added preflight step to canonicalize weight shard ordering and metadata serialization to address nondeterminism.
2025-03-02: Safety team provided baseline toxic-output classifier and license heuristics for pipeline integration; flagged models with incompatible licenses.
2025-03-03: First end-to-end smoke run completed for community-model-2025-02; compatibility tests showed a failed kernel on older CUDA drivers — fallback path will be implemented.
design_decisions: Use signed-manifests with SHA-256 checksums rather than ad-hoc zip uploads to simplify provenance and re-run determinism.
Conversion worker will run as idempotent tasks in Kubernetes with a deterministic seed for any random ops and strict serialization of metadata to ensure reproducible hashes.
Pin recommendation will be a rules + telemetry hybrid: rules encode hard constraints (license, safety), telemetry scores determine preferred runtime/quantization for cost/latency tradeoffs.
Profiles are versioned semantically (major.minor.build) and immutable once published; profile publisher must support soft-deprecations and roll-forward aliases.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Non-deterministic conversion leading to inconsistent runtime behavior. Mitigation: canonical shard ordering, deterministic PRNG seeds, and independent double-run verification.
Risk: Safety classifier false positives blocking legitimate community models. Mitigation: surface explainability in console, allow manual override via escalation workflow with audit logging.
Risk: Long-running compatibility tests delaying publish. Mitigation: run fast smoke tests first and publish provisional profile with canary restriction until full suite completes.
Risk: License or export restrictions discovered late. Mitigation: upfront license scan and required uploader attestations on manifest submission.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and license scanner
Two independent end-to-end conversion runs must compare equal hashes
Compatibility smoke: generate token-level outputs for 10 short prompts and verify checksum of KV-cache access patterns
Safety regression: run toxic-output classifier on 1000 synthetic prompts and ensure no model is false-blocked without audit
Canary deploy: publish provisional profile to a 1% traffic slice on dedicated capacity and monitor error/latency for 48h
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): publish provisional profile with canary=1% to dedicated workers; monitor for 48 hours
Phase 2 (ramped): if canary stable, increase to 10% for 24 hours and run full compatibility suite in background
Phase 3 (full publish): promote profile to general catalog and allow pinned deployments; tag previous profile as deprecated but recoverable
Emergency rollback: profile publisher can mark profile as revoked and automatically redirect runtime traffic to fallback stable variant
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on determinism controls in conversion worker and how we capture provenance in the manifest — we need guarantees for reproducible hashes.
Safety team: review classifier thresholds and escalation workflow wording so we avoid unnecessary model churn.
Runtime team: validate suggested runtime targets and quantization knobs in the pin payload match available kernels.
